clue.text: One vessel in front of another on loch

blocks.note: the bow is the front part of a ship, another vessel
L is the map abbreviation for loch or lake

explanation.surface: One boat moored ahead of a second on a Scottish lake.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Vessel' tempts you to read every word as shipping, but the answer is a kitchen vessel; only the front of a ship supplies letters.
explanation.definitionFit: A bowl is a round container, and any container for food or liquid can be called a vessel.

clue.text: What could be done by changing past

indicators.note: changing the words means shifting their letters into a new arrangement

blocks.note: taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: A rueful thought about what might have been achieved if history could be altered.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Past' looks like a noun meaning history; it is the preposition, as in 'past the church'.
explanation.definitionFit: Beyond and past both mean further on than some point, as prepositions or adverbs.

clue.text: Left in part of hospital, given old-fashioned medical treatment

indicators.note: one thing being in another means it sits inside the other's letters

blocks.note: a hospital bed, one unit of its capacity
L is the standard abbreviation for left

explanation.surface: A patient abandoned on a ward and subjected to antiquated medicine.
explanation.definitionFit: Bloodletting was the old cure-all, so a patient who was bled received that outdated treatment.

clue.text: Like many retired people, please put in revised order

indicators.note: putting something in a revised order rearranges its letters into a fresh sequence

blocks.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A request, perhaps from pensioners, to have something sorted again.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Retired' suggests pensioners; here it means gone to bed for the night.
explanation.definitionFit: People who have retired for the night have gone to bed, and most of them will be sleeping.

clue.text: Upset if senior figures cover points, for example

indicators.note: something upset is knocked over, so its letters fall into a different order

blocks.note: taken as written
elders are senior members of a community or church

explanation.surface: A worry that senior people might be upset by a rule covering certain points.
explanation.walkthrough: Cover point is a fielding position in cricket, so the players stationed there are examples of the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: In cricket, players placed around the field to stop the ball are fielders, and cover point is one such position.

clue.text: Something one has put on show, initially, before meeting

indicators.note: initially points to the opening letter of each of the preceding words

blocks.note: the first letters of the three words
a session is a meeting of a body such as a council or court

explanation.surface: Something a person has displayed before attending a gathering.
explanation.definitionFit: A possession is an item that belongs to someone, a thing that a person owns.

clue.text: Old volume found in particular joint

indicators.note: being found in something means sitting inside its letters

blocks.note: a particular is a detail, as in 'in every particular'
O is the abbreviation for old
V is the abbreviation for volume

explanation.surface: An old book discovered in a specific pub or eatery.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Joint' reads as a pub or restaurant; it is the woodworking joint.
explanation.definitionFit: A dovetail is an interlocking woodworking joint with flared tenons fitting into matching slots.

clue.text: Part of pageant I warmly dedicated to peace

indicators.note: part of tells you only a stretch of the following words is wanted

blocks.note: runs across the end of the first word, the lone letter and the start of the third

explanation.surface: A section of a pageant was warmly devoted to the cause of peace.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone opposed to war is committed to peace, so an antiwar stance is dedicated to it.

clue.text: Man trying to attract woman with diamonds, say, and gold

blocks.note: diamonds is one example of a suit of cards
or is the heraldic term for gold

explanation.surface: A man wooing a woman with diamonds and gold.
explanation.walkthrough: The jewellery surface is apt, but diamonds is a suit of cards and gold is the heraldic colour.
explanation.definitionFit: A suitor is a man who courts a woman, hoping to win her affection or hand.

clue.text: Practically nothing received by charity ahead of time

indicators.note: something received by another is taken inside it

blocks.note: alms are charitable gifts to the poor
O is zero, nothing
T is the abbreviation for time

explanation.surface: A charity gets next to nothing before a deadline.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Practically nothing' reads as one phrase; the definition is the first word alone.
explanation.definitionFit: Almost and practically both mean very nearly, not quite completely.

clue.text: Fighter that's outstanding, large and lean

blocks.note: a debt that is outstanding is due
L is the clothing-size abbreviation for large
a ship that lists leans to one side

explanation.surface: A boxer who is excellent, big and trim.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Outstanding' and 'lean' both look like compliments to a physique; one means unpaid, the other means tilt.
explanation.definitionFit: A duellist fights formal one-to-one combats, so is a kind of fighter.

clue.text: They can have views without buying lies about popular party points

definitions.text: They can have views without buying

indicators.note: about means going round, so one set of letters encloses the rest

blocks.note: whoppers are big lies
in means fashionable, popular
a do is a party
two compass points, west and south

explanation.surface: Voters seeing through a populist party's lies on policy points.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Views' suggests opinions; it means looking at goods in shop windows.
explanation.definitionFit: Window-shoppers browse displays in shop windows without purchasing anything.

clue.text: Not just occupying one South American city, also part of North America

blocks.note: occupying a place means being in it
I is the Roman numeral one
Quito is the capital of Ecuador
the United States

explanation.surface: A geography question about occupying a South American city and a North American country.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Occupying' looks like a container indicator but here simply gives the word in.
explanation.definitionFit: Something iniquitous is grossly unfair or wicked, so it is not just in the moral sense.

clue.text: Mannerism seen in husband, to some extent

blocks.note: H is the abbreviation for husband
a bit means to some extent

explanation.surface: A quirk noticed in one's spouse, at least partly.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Seen in' and 'to some extent' both hint at hidden words, but this is a straight build.
explanation.definitionFit: A habit is a regular tendency or characteristic way of behaving, much like a mannerism.

clue.text: Audible disapproval in this snigger or sigh is strong

indicators.note: in tells you the letters lie inside the words that follow

blocks.note: runs from the second letter of the first word into the start of the second

explanation.surface: Disapproval you can hear in a snigger or a heavy sigh.
explanation.walkthrough: The answer is concealed twice: once across 'this snigger' and again across 'sigh is strong'; either stretch alone solves it.
explanation.definitionFit: Audiences hiss to show disapproval, a sharp sibilant sound of contempt.

clue.text: Bad miss when holding prized weapons

indicators.note: bad suggests something gone wrong, so the letters are muddled
holding something means wrapping round it

blocks.note: taken as written
something prized is dear

explanation.surface: Valued firearms that shoot wide of the target.
explanation.definitionFit: Sidearms are weapons worn at the side, such as pistols or swords.

clue.text: Rise as bandleader in middle of dance

indicators.note: in the middle of means placed inside, with letters either side

blocks.note: a reel is a lively Scottish dance
the leading letter of band

explanation.surface: A band's conductor gets up halfway through a dance.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Bandleader' looks like a person; it is just the first letter of band, a common crossword trick.
explanation.definitionFit: To rebel is to rise up against authority, as in an uprising.

clue.text: Catcher of fish in lake before day's end — matter of luck

indicators.note: the end of a word is its final letter

blocks.note: L is the abbreviation for lake
an otter is a river mammal that catches fish
the final letter of day

explanation.surface: Catching fish in a lake before nightfall is all down to chance.
explanation.walkthrough: The block order follows the answer: lake comes first though the clue mentions it second.
explanation.definitionFit: A lottery is anything decided by pure chance, so it is a matter of luck.

clue.text: Unhappy after the speaker's been introduced and spoke

indicators.note: something introduced is put inside, here inside the word for unhappy

blocks.note: sad means unhappy
the speaker refers to himself or herself as I

explanation.surface: Someone spoke glumly after a speaker was introduced.
explanation.definitionFit: Said is the past tense of say, so it means spoke or uttered.

clue.text: Turned out to cover people on condition it avoids stress

indicators.note: out suggests something put out of its usual order
to cover means to go around and enclose other letters
in an across clue, one word on another means it follows it, so the word for people comes second

blocks.note: taken as written
a state is a condition
men are people

explanation.surface: Something turned out to protect people provided it causes no strain.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Stress' sounds like strain; it is emphasis, which an understatement deliberately avoids.
explanation.definitionFit: An understatement presents something as less than it is, so it plays down rather than emphasises.

clue.text: Engineers serving wine or pop

blocks.note: RE is the Royal Engineers, a British army corps
port is a fortified wine

explanation.surface: Soldiers serving drinks, either wine or fizzy pop.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Pop' looks like a soft drink to match the wine; it is the sound of a bang.
explanation.definitionFit: A report is the sharp sound of a gunshot or explosion, much like a pop or bang.

clue.text: It is in city centre

blocks.note: surface reading: something located downtown
setter's reading: the letters I and T sit at the core of the word city

explanation.walkthrough: Read literally, the two letters 'it' sit in the heart of the word 'city', so the clue points at the position they occupy.
explanation.definitionFit: The centre of something is its midpoint, the place halfway between the edges.

clue.text: Goes back without penny, so short of cash

indicators.note: back means the word is read from its end to its start
without in its old sense of outside, so these letters go round another

blocks.note: departs means goes away
P is the abbreviation for penny

explanation.surface: Someone returns home without a penny, so is broke.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Without' looks like 'lacking'; here it means outside, wrapping round the coin.
explanation.definitionFit: Strapped is informal for short of money, as in 'strapped for cash'.

clue.text: Sewer's repair producing angry pronouncement

blocks.note: first meaning: a mend made by stitching across a hole
second meaning: a mild curse, a polite substitute for damn

explanation.surface: Mending a garment leads someone to swear.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Sewer' could be a drain; it is someone who sews.
explanation.definitionFit: A darn is a woven patch over a hole in fabric, and darn is also a mild oath.

clue.text: Conclusion still to be decided without pressure up front

indicators.note: without the front pressure means its opening letter is dropped

blocks.note: a matter still to be decided is pending
P is the symbol for pressure

explanation.surface: A conclusion left open, without anyone pushing for it.
explanation.definitionFit: An ending is the final part of something, its conclusion.

clue.text: Child brought up on hot food

indicators.note: in a down entry, brought up means the word is read from bottom to top

blocks.note: a son is a child
H is the tap abbreviation for hot

explanation.surface: A child raised on hot meals.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Brought up' suggests raising a child; it is the upward reversal. In a down clue, 'on' means placed above.
explanation.definitionFit: Nosh is informal British slang for food.

clue.text: Drink repeatedly passed around, say, quietly

indicators.note: passed around suggests turning a thing round so it faces the other way

blocks.note: rum, a spirit, written twice

explanation.surface: A drink is handed round again and again, and someone comments in a low voice.
explanation.definitionFit: To murmur is to utter something in a low, soft voice.

clue.text: A Tory is oddly accepting line that was opposing Parliament

indicators.note: oddly means in a strange way, so the letters are put into an odd order
accepting means taking in another letter

blocks.note: taken as written
L is the abbreviation for line

explanation.surface: A Conservative is strangely sympathetic to a party line against Parliament.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Oddly' looks like it selects odd letters, but here it scrambles them. In the English Civil War, Royalists fought Parliament's forces.
explanation.definitionFit: Royalists supported Charles I against the Parliamentarians in the English Civil War.
